title: Compatible geometric compactifications of a composable pair
statement: Let $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z$ be separated finite-type morphisms of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $d=(i:Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y,\overline g:\overline Y\to Z)$ be a compactification of $g$ [def-nagata-compactification]. There exists a compactification $e=(a:X\hookrightarrow\overline X,p:\overline X\to\overline Y)$ of $i\circ f$. Put $U=\overline X\times_{\overline Y}Y$, with projections $b:U\to\overline X$ and $p_Y:U\to Y$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. There is a quasi-compact open immersion $c:X\hookrightarrow U$ with $b\circ c=a$ and $p_Y\circ c=f$. The morphism $b$ is a quasi-compact open immersion and $p_Y$ is proper. Both $(c,p_Y)$ and $(a,\overline g\circ p)$ are compactifications, of $f$ and $g\circ f$ respectively. The square $p\circ b=i\circ p_Y$ is Cartesian.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, label lemma-shriek-composition, proof: first paragraph and displayed compactification diagram

proof.text: Unpack $d$: $i$ is a quasi-compact open immersion, $\overline g$ is proper, and $\overline g i=g$. Properness makes $\overline g$ quasi-compact and separated. Its diagonal is therefore a closed immersion, hence proper by clause (c) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], hence quasi-compact by the definition of proper and finite type. Thus $\overline g$ is quasi-separated. Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] to $\overline g$ and the qcqs scheme $Z$: $\overline Y$ is qcqs.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, lemma-shriek-composition, proof first paragraph and compactification diagram; hypotheses for the second compactification; Schemes Tag 01KU and the definition of quasi-separated

proof.text: Put $h=i\circ f$. By [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type], $i$ is of finite type. Clause (e) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] gives that $h$ is locally of finite type; clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] makes it quasi-compact, since $X$ is quasi-compact and $\overline Y$ is quasi-separated. Hence $h$ is of finite type. An open immersion is a monomorphism: maps into its source are determined by their composites with the inclusion of the open subscheme. Consequently $X\times_Y X\cong X\times_{\overline Y}X$: for every test scheme the conditions $f u=f v$ and $i f u=i f v$ are equivalent, and the inverse morphisms are the pairs of projections supplied by the fibre-product universal property. Under these inverse maps the diagonals agree. Since the diagonal of $f$ is a closed immersion, so is that of $h$; thus $h$ is separated.

proof.text: Apply [thm-nagata-compactification] to $h:X\to\overline Y$: step 1 supplies its qcqs base and step 2 supplies separatedness and finite type. Obtain a compactification $e=(a:X\hookrightarrow\overline X,p:\overline X\to\overline Y)$, with $p a=i f$, $a$ a quasi-compact open immersion and $p$ proper.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, lemma-shriek-composition, proof first paragraph and compactification diagram; second sentence; More on Flatness Tag 0F41, theorem-nagata

proof.text: Form $U=\overline X\times_{\overline Y}Y$ with projections $b,p_Y$. Its defining equality is $p b=i p_Y$, and its defining universal property says that this square is Cartesian. The pair $(a,f)$ defines $c:X\to U$ with $bc=a$ and $p_Yc=f$. Base change $e$ along $i$. By [def-nagata-compactification-base-change] and [lemma-nagata-compactification-base-change], the resulting factorization $X\times_{\overline Y}Y\to U\to Y$ is a compactification of $X\times_{\overline Y}Y\to Y$. Identify its source with $X$ explicitly: the forward map is $(1_X,f)$, the inverse is the first projection. In the fibre product $i\operatorname{pr}_Y=i f\operatorname{pr}_X$, so monicity of the open immersion $i$ gives $\operatorname{pr}_Y=f\operatorname{pr}_X$; the two composites are identities by uniqueness in the fibre-product universal property. Under this identification the first map is exactly $c$, since its projections are $a,f$, and the second is $p_Y$. Therefore $c$ is a quasi-compact open immersion and $p_Y$ is proper, and $(c,p_Y)$ compactifies $f$.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, lemma-shriek-composition, proof first paragraph and compactification diagram; inverse image U and the left triangle in the displayed diagram

proof.text: The projection $b$ is the base change of $i$ along $p$, hence is an open immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] and quasi-compact by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Finally $\overline g\circ p$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition], and $(\overline g\circ p)\circ a=\overline g\circ(i\circ f)=g\circ f$. Together with the quasi-compact open immersion $a$ this is precisely the compactification $(a,\overline g\circ p)$ of $g\circ f$. All asserted equations and the Cartesian square were obtained in step 4.
